$comment: The Merlin Agent macOS collection manifest.
THIS FILE IS THE COMPLETE LIST OF WHAT THE AGENT READS ON macOS. Every query below runs
through osqueryi and nothing else is collected. An administrator can paste any of them into
osqueryi on their own Mac and get byte-identical output — which is a far stronger assurance
than reading the agent's source, and is the main reason collection is delegated to osquery
rather than hand-rolled.
NOTHING HERE READS WHO IS SIGNED IN. There is no query for the console user, the session or
any mail address. The `screenlock` query is the one place a per-user setting is even nearby,
and osquery resolves it internally without ever returning a username — see its own comment.
macOS EXPOSES LESS AT MACHINE SCOPE THAN WINDOWS DOES, and the gaps are left as gaps. The
screen-lock idle interval, patch currency and antimalware signature age have no machine-wide
source on a Mac without an MDM, so they are not collected and Merlin reports them as not
observed. A query that guessed at them would be worse than the silence.
A query that fails or returns nothing produces a NULL reading, never a false one. Merlin
treats null as 'not observed' and will not raise a nonconformity from it.

QUERIES RUN IN THE ORDER LISTED HERE, AND THE ORDER IS DELIBERATE. A collection is bounded so it cannot hold the machine lock past the point where the updater gives up waiting for it, and on a machine where osquery answers slowly that bound is reached before the end of this list. Whatever is left is reported as NOT OBSERVED, so the security-posture queries come first and the inventory ones last: losing a hostname degrades a device page, while losing disk encryption or the firewall loses the reading the ISMS exists to take.
A PRIVACY-CRITICAL QUERY. The disk_encryption table also carries `uid` and `user_uuid` —
'currently authenticated user if available' — which identify the person who unlocked the
volume. This query names exactly the columns it wants, so those are never returned to the
agent at all: the restriction is enforced by the query rather than by the agent
remembering to ignore them, the same way the Windows pack restricts the Entra join info.
NOT JOINED TO mounts, deliberately. Scoping to the root volume reads better but does not
survive contact with modern macOS: the system volume is a sealed snapshot (disk3s1s1)
while the data volume is separate (disk3s5), so a join on the mounted device matches
nothing on an APFS Mac and every machine would report encryption as 'not observed'.
FileVault is a whole-machine setting, so the normaliser reduces all rows to one
machine-level answer instead.
filevault.sql: SELECT name, encrypted, encryption_status, filevault_status, type FROM disk_encryption;
filevault.purpose: Whether this Mac is protected by FileVault (A.8.24).

gatekeeper.purpose: Whether Gatekeeper refuses unsigned and un-notarised code — macOS's malware-prevention control (A.8.7). Signature currency is NOT collected: XProtect updates through a channel with no locally readable 'current' version to compare against.

alf.purpose: The macOS application firewall. 0 is off; 1 and 2 are both on, differing only in strictness.

sip.sql: SELECT enabled FROM sip_config WHERE config_flag = 'sip';
sip.purpose: System Integrity Protection — macOS's verified-boot equivalent, reported as the Secure Boot signal.

$comment: THE PRIVACY-SENSITIVE QUERY. Whether the screen requires a password is a per-user
preference, and osquery resolves the console user's setting internally — this table
returns only `enabled` and `grace_period`, with no username, uid or session in its
output. The agent therefore never handles an identity even though the value originates
in a user's own domain.
grace_period IS COLLECTED BUT NOT REPORTED AS THE LOCK TIMEOUT. It is the delay after
the screensaver starts, not the idle time before it does, so sending it as the timeout
would understate a machine's exposure. It appears here so the manifest matches what the
query actually returns.
screenlock.purpose: Whether unlocking this Mac requires a password (A.7.7 clear screen). Expect NO ROWS in normal operation: osquery reads this from the current logged-in user context, and the agent runs as root from a launch daemon which has none. That is why Merlin usually shows this signal as not observed on a Mac.

$comment: Returns LOCAL ACCOUNT names, not the identity of whoever is signed in. A.8.2 is
materially weaker without them: a count says there are four administrators but not that
one of them is unexpected.
local_admins.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN user_groups ug ON u.uid = ug.uid JOIN groups g ON ug.gid = g.gid WHERE g.groupname = 'admin';

os_version.sql: SELECT name, version, build, platform FROM os_version;
os_version.purpose: macOS name, version and build — what end-of-support is judged against.

system_volume.sql: SELECT blocks, blocks_available, blocks_size FROM mounts WHERE path = '/';
system_volume.purpose: Free space on the system volume (A.8.6 capacity).

system_info.sql: SELECT hostname, uuid, hardware_serial, hardware_vendor, hardware_model, cpu_brand FROM system_info;
system_info.purpose: Machine identity, the serial used to reconcile against the asset register, and the CPU brand that establishes whether this Mac has a Secure Enclave.
